Document Center

Generate the Central Document Center folder structure

Step 3 of 8 · Document Center folder import

Build folders from the navigation tree

The generator uses the consolidated site map from Step 2 and the current Page/Microsite exports. It creates a navigation folder only when that page or one of its descendants references a migratable asset. Regular files go to Document Center; image files go to Image Repository. Module, external, and duplicate/linked rows are excluded.

Folder structure preview

Folder titles are unique within each repository. The canonical occurrence keeps its title; later occurrences receive [Dupe 1], [Dupe 2], and so on. Parent Folder values use the final unique title required by the import.

File NameFolder NameParent Folder NameAlt TextDisplay NameDescription

Import CSVs match the confirmed DocumentCenter/ImageRepository template: File Name, Folder Name, Parent Folder Name, Alt Text, Display Name, Description. One row per file — folders with no files of their own aren't representable in this format, but are still created implicitly whenever referenced as a deeper file's Parent Folder Name.

Strict source scope: current published Bids/RFPs records only.

Resource Directory

Map current published Business Listings into the Central Resource Directory import format

Step 4 of 8 · Resource Directory import
Strict source scope: current published Business Listings only (189 of 194 on the site this was validated against).

This is a tab-delimited .txt file, not a CSV — a genuinely different format from every other module in this tool. Empty required fields must contain a literal space (not left blank), and no blank lines are allowed anywhere in the file. Categories are variable-width trailing fields, one per column, not a fixed column.

Import mapping

Required: Business Name = title. Address resolves field_address directly, falling back to the referenced Standard Location if the listing has no direct address of its own. Link to Map = 1 when field_map_options is "address" and a real address resolved. Link = field_website_link, falling back to Facebook → Instagram → Twitter → YouTube when there's no website (confirmed only 8 of 194 records would otherwise lose their only link) — Link Text is fixed to "Visit Website", Open in New Window fixed to 1, whenever a Link is present. Description embeds the primary image (left-justified, inline) the same way Bids/Jobs do, then body, truncated to Central's enforced 1000-character limit with the image tag always kept intact. Categories resolve field_business_category to real names (e.g. "Lodging", "Restaurants") as trailing fields. Contact Person Name, Ext, and Fax Number stay blank — confirmed no source field exists for any of them in this content type.

Business NameAddress 1CityStateZipMapPhoneEmailLinkDescriptionCategoriesReview

Downloads as tab-delimited .txt, matching Central's exact required format (17 fixed fields, then variable-width category fields). The review column above is not part of the output file.

Facilities (Parks)

Map current published Parks into the Central Facilities import template

Step 4 of 8 · Facilities import
Strict source scope: current published Parks only. No reservation functionality exists on the Drupal side at all.

Category is fixed to "Parks"; Allow Public/Automatic Reservations fixed to "No" (the customer can turn this on later now that Central actually supports it). Description reuses the exact same pipeline as Pages/News/Calendar (buildFullText) — primary image, body, any embedded-page teaser cards in field_sections, and a Supporting Documents list from field_file_attachments if present — rather than the simpler image+body pattern used for Bids/Jobs, since Parks genuinely has the same embedded-content capability Pages does.

Confirmed against the actual Central help documentation: Facilities has no bulk-import mechanism for Related Documents or Slideshow images at all — both are manual, per-facility actions in Central's own admin UI. Files land correctly in Document Center via Step 3; the connection to a specific Facility has to be made by hand afterward. The worklist below names the exact file for each facility that needs one, so that manual step doesn't require hunting for it.

Import mapping

Required: Facility Name = title. Address resolves field_address directly (no Standard Location reference exists on Parks). Specify Hours of Operation fixed to "No" since the source is always freeform text, never day-by-day — that text goes to Hours of Operation Note instead. FEATURE1–25 = field_amenities resolved to real names, one per column. Parent Facility Name, Admission Fee, Max Number of People, Contact info, Video, Web Address, Has Calendar, Show Directions (all three), and Display Start/End Date all stay blank — confirmed no source field exists for any of them.

Import workspace

Meetings Embed

Meeting scope

Only meetings with a Drupal-hosted agenda, minutes, or packet file are included. Meetings whose only agenda/minutes/packet content is a third-party link (NovusAgenda, Municode Meetings) are excluded here -- that content is handled separately via Meetings Embed.

Known limitations

Workflow

1. Create the categories in Central

The import does not create categories. Create and publish each one below in Central, named exactly as shown, before importing anything.

2. Review what will be held back (optional, best before importing)

3. Download the import workbook

Saves to your Downloads folder as -Master_Content_Import.xlsx. Leave it there; the next step looks for it.

4. Build the import zip

Download the script, open PowerShell, and paste the whole script in. It downloads every file from the old site, adds the No Agenda template if needed, and builds -agenda-center-import.zip in your Downloads folder, then opens Downloads with the zip selected. Files to attach by hand after import (the official minutes, plus any items held back by same-date collisions) go in -agenda-center-attach-after-import. Working files live in your temp folder and are removed afterward. The zip is always built: a file that can't be downloaded (removed from the old site, behind a login, or not a real file) is left out and listed in -agenda-center-file-log.csv in your Downloads folder, with the meeting it belongs to and its source URL, so you can fetch it by hand and add it to the zip.

5. Import the zip in Central, then publish

Import -agenda-center-import.zip, then publish the imported meetings. Imported meetings arrive as drafts.

6. Finish what the importer can't do

Upload the Drupal Webform YAML exports. These definitions provide the authoritative open/closed state and identify forms that may exist only through the legacy Forms view.

Equivalent / previous site domains

Optional — one hostname or full domain URL per line. Links using these domains are treated as internal and rewritten to the live domain detected from the homepage HTML. Any civicpluswebopen.com preview or staging subdomain is recognized automatically; enter only additional former or custom production domains.

Module link patterns

Links matching these paths get classified as "Linked Page" (module views, not real page content) rather than content to migrate. Edit as needed for this site — one per line, as /path=Label.

Menu consolidation review

Choose the menu's existing landing page when it is already in the tree, or choose the parent location where a missing landing page belongs. The tool will add that landing page first and place its Drupal children one tier beneath it. Children of unresolved menus are held out of orphan review so they are not added twice.

Auxiliary link cross-references

Header/footer/key-link items that duplicate existing content or a module. Not added as tree rows.

Subsites to consolidate

For each subsite homepage uploaded above, pick which section it belongs to. Consolidating replaces that section's raw structure with a properly-organized tree built the same way the main site was, using this subsite's own navigation as the skeleton.

Live /forms page HTML

Save-As the site's live /forms page. If it's paginated, Save-As every page (?page=0, ?page=1, etc.) and upload them all together. When provided, this becomes the authoritative source for which orphaned pages belong under Forms — replacing the need to manually confirm individual webforms as open or closed.

Pages not in sitemap

Published internal regular Pages not represented in the consolidated tree. Current node records are scanned for references, including their currently attached sections and paragraphs; standalone Paragraphs export rows are not used because they can belong only to an old page revision. A Page is auto-placed only beneath a referring page already in the tree. If several tree pages refer to it, its URL alias may break the tie only among those actual referring pages; otherwise it requires review. References from content outside the tree are shown as context. External redirects, module paths, News, Calendar Events, and Forms directory items are excluded.

Export summary

Review & assign years

Central needs a tab per year. Year is taken from Adopted Date, falling back to Public Hearing Date, then Introduction Date, then Postponed Until. Rows with none of the four go to an "Other Years" table unless you assign one here.

Interpolates from nearby ordinance/resolution numbers with a known year. Always double-check estimates.
TypeNo.TitleDate sourceYear

Generate tables

One HTML table per year, split by Ordinance/Resolution. Anything still without a year lands in a separate "Other Years" table, sorted by No. highest to lowest. A column only appears in a given year's table if at least one row in that year actually has a value for it. Document links point to the original site's files for now — those get downloaded, re-hosted in Central's Document Center, and relinked automatically as part of the API import, the same as News and Events.

Sort each year's table by

"Other Years" always sorts by No. highest to lowest, regardless of this setting, since those rows don't have a reliable date.

Columns to consider

Title is always shown. Everything below is included automatically only where it has data — untick anything you want left out no matter what. "ID" and "Status" render as "Ordinance ID"/"Ordinance Status" or "Resolution ID"/"Resolution Status" depending on which table they're in.

"Queue for Pages processing" just marks these tables as ready and timestamps them for now — there's no Pages-processing step to hand off to yet. Once that's built, this is the intended connection point.
